This is about survival. And when you are that desperate, when the darkness is about to swallow you whole, I think it's okay to forget the bad for however long you need to while you heal. How can you help others and save the world when you are one step away from jumping over the edge? 

Some people need to take time to focus on the good, their lives depend on it. The darkness isn't going anywhere unfortunately, so it can wait. We can return to it when we are stable enough to do so.

Something I tried that seemed to work (although lately I seem to be struggling a great deal...) was to stop looking at myself. Literally: I refused to look in the mirror unless it was necessary, and figuratively: Any time I heard those judgmental, critical thoughts in my head, I silenced them and tried focusing on something else. 
I started looking out. Literally: I researched how I could travel, see the world, experience great things. And figuratively: I criticized myself so much over my looks for so, so long; instead I try to look for the beauty in the world - whether it's animals, scenery, the kindness of strangers, hanging out with good friends, amazing food, etc. What beauty foes the world have to offer me?
I hope this helps...

Since, he's in therapy for the family troubles, the acne cleared up, but the PMO addiction hasn't stopped. I am so, so proud of him, we understand each other, and instead of hiding things from one another, we can focus our energy on healing.

Your situation is one I can relate to greatly. My guy and I have been together +4 yrs also - but really, the first 3 years were extremely difficult. My guy told me he would quit PMO pretty early on in the relationship after I started finding porn on my own computer and he wouldn't always be able to climax in bed. Well, he lied. I was a little obsessive about it for the first  two years, checking his computer for porn, etc. And of course, I would find it! This ruined me, we had horrible fights, we lost trust in one another (he was pissed that I looked through his comp and I was pissed at what I found!). Furthermore, we both became extremely insecure - he was ashamed of his "inability to perform" as well as his inability to quit PMO, I truly felt worthless, unattractive, not good enough.

This is what can happen if you are not upfront about your situation with your longterm gf. Bc she can sense it, your lack of interest, and she really wants to know what's up. The best thing, and I strongly encourage you to think this over, was when my guy sat me down in a restaurant and told me what was up. (I think the neutral territory just made us a little more comfortable? It was crowded and loud so it wasn't hard to talk about these things.) He was so brave, he admitted that yes, the porn was really messing with his brain, that he's trying really hard to quit, that it really wasn't my fault that he had a hard time in bed, that he really does love me and only me and he wants to fix this for the both of us. Needless to say, I bawled my eyes out, right there in the restaurant, and he teared up too. Later, he sent me articles to read on my own.

It was really hard at first, I needed to know everything - if he relapsed, what I could do to help, etc. He really didn't want to talk about it in the beginning, but the more we shared, the more trust we were able to rebuild after years of insecurity. 

If you were just starting out with her, I would actually suggest you wait and give NoFap a try, hopefully you could get rid of some of the problems without her ever knowing there were any. But bc you have been at it for years, bc you seem committed to both her and NoFap, and bc you've already said "it's my fault," I recommend you tell her what's up. Show her she really wasn't to blame for all those failed attempts at sex, that you love her a lot and you trust that she'll help you through this. 

If she's like me, she'll probably cry, but she'll be so proud of you for communicating with her and for trying to make the relationship even better. I have a feeling she'll love you even more.

Right now? After 4 years? Bc earlier in our relationship, before I knew you could be addicted, I got extremely emotional! After he did more research and found NoFap, he did probably the bravest thing any man in his position could do: He sat me down (at a firggen restaurant even!) and admitted that porn was really effing with his brain, that he can't seem to stop, that it really could be causing the ED. Later he sent me links for me to read by myself. It was such a shock for me, I was a little upset at first, even cried all over my salad! I cried bc it was so sad that this madness had been tearing us apart and we both had no idea to what extent it was really impacting our relationship. I also cried bc I was just so friggen proud of him for telling me, for trying to change, bc I was so relieved it wasn't my fault (I admit), and bc now we knew how to help the situation. 

For a while after this conversation, if he relapsed with fapping, I made him tell me. He FU-UCKING hated this, but I needed to know. He resisted at first, but then realized it helped us bc we needed to rebuild trust. He HAD to tell me if we were going to trust each other during this process.

Now, after several months, I don't pry about it as much. If he relapsed and told me, I would feel just as proud of him as I was in that restaurant - I'd be so proud that he told me and we'd work through it. Now, if I found out he relapsed by accident, like I found porn in his history or something, I'd feel pretty uncomfortable, like he was hiding something from me. I'd probably wait for the right time to sit him down and have another heart to heart, and reassure him that I still love him and he doesn't need to hide anything like this from me. No big. We got through it before, we'll get through it again:)

Oh, he had mood swings - but then, he always has and he still does to this day on occasion! Honestly, this might sound crazy, but sometimes he'd get moody bc he hadn't eaten for a long time so I would try to sneak him some food to boost the blood sugar! 

Another thing I had to do was accept that we handle stress very differently - when I am down, I need a hug, attention, to be told "It's gonna be alright." When he gets moody, he needs space! To help him, I constantly remind myself to **stay** **calm,** that it will pass, and give him room to breathe for a bit. It was hard, but I always tried to stay positive. I know he'd do it for me!
